title: DMC3 HD table extents corrected against absorbed pools and record interiors

records.title: The pitch of constant references measures a table's real element size
records.summary: A constant index folded into a displacement makes every reference an exact byte offset into the table, so the spacing of those offsets is a measurement of the element size that is independent of anything read from the bytes. Where the two disagree the byte reading is wrong. Two runs disagreed: at RVA 0x36F288 and at RVA 0x506F68 the references ran at a pitch of eight under a declared stride of sixteen, and the scan had to record every second one as landing eight bytes inside an element. Neither run is indexed at eight throughout; in both the pitch changes partway, and the point at which it changes is the end of the real table. This is a cheap check that needs no new analysis, only the references already recovered, and it is the check that would have caught the blind spot recorded in dmc3-hdc-table-indices without waiting for anyone to doubt the result.

locations.symbol: run whose reference pitch contradicted its stride
locations.note: RVA 0x506F68, declared stride 16 over 22 elements. References at offsets 0 through 240 run at a pitch of 16; from offset 256 they run at a pitch of 8.

locations.symbol: run whose reference pitch contradicted its stride
locations.note: RVA 0x36F288, declared stride 16 over 30 elements. References at offsets 456, 464 and 472 run at a pitch of 8.

records.title: A grid runs off its table into the pool that follows it
records.summary: The blind spot recorded earlier is not a pool that resembles a table; it is a real table whose extent ran past its own end. A pool of short names is padded to the same alignment the grid uses, so the grid keeps validating after the table has ended, and because the pool's own strings fall at a fixed sub-multiple of the stride the payload offsets stay consistent and the existing pool rejection never fires. What separates the two is where payload appears: an element of a name table is a name and NUL padding, so payload can only appear once the grid has left the table, as an unbroken run at the end. Payload from the first element is a record whose second field the constant-stride scan cannot see, and trimming that would delete a real table, so the rule requires a strict suffix containing at least one text payload. Applying it corrects RVA 0x506F68 from 22 elements to 16 and RVA 0x36F288 from 30 to 28, and trims two further runs, removing 14 absorbed elements in total across four runs of 223.

locations.note: RVA 0x506F68, stride 16, corrected from 22 elements to 16. The corrected run is a pure name array; sample name FogColor.
RVA 0x36F288, stride 16, corrected from 30 elements to 28. Sample name Maguma.ogg.

records.title: The absorbed tail is a table in its own right
records.summary: Trimming does not consume the elements it removes, so the scan reads the region again on its own terms. The tail taken off RVA 0x506F68 is recovered as a separate run at RVA 0x507068 with a stride of eight and 11 entries, and every one of those entries is named by a constant index from two functions. That is the strongest confirmation available for both readings at once: the pitch of eight that contradicted the old stride is the new run's declared stride, and the contradiction disappears. Across the image the references that had to be recorded as landing inside an element fall from 16 to 7, and the total number of references rises from 202 to 206. The seven that remain sit at offsets of 13, 16 and 20 under strides of 16 and 24, which is not the sub-multiple pitch of an absorbed pool and points at genuine field access within a record.

locations.symbol: table recovered from a trimmed tail
locations.note: RVA 0x507068, stride 8, 11 entries, all 11 named by a constant index from 2 functions.

locations.symbol: table adjacent to a corrected extent
locations.note: RVA 0x506E88, stride 16, 9 entries, all 9 named by a constant index.

records.title: How to read a table's coverage, with payload-bearing runs settled
records.summary: The earlier reading held that coverage measured over a payload-bearing run is an upper bound until the extent is confirmed independently. That caveat can now be discharged for the two runs it was written about. RVA 0x506F68 read 22 of 22 elements covered; corrected to 16 elements it reads 16 of 16, and the tail that inflated the count is its own fully covered table. The caveat itself stands and is worth keeping: coverage is trustworthy where the extent is, and the reference pitch is what settles the extent.

locations.note: RVA 0x506F68, stride 16, 16 entries, all 16 named by a constant index from 2 functions.

records.title: Most recovered runs are a record's interior, not a table
records.summary: A record whose name fields are all one width contains a constant-stride grid by construction, so the two scans describe the same bytes and report them twice. 179 of 223 runs coincide with a contiguous block of equal-width fields in one of the 25 recovered record layouts, leaving 44 that stand on their own. The record array at RVA 0x35D640 alone accounts for 20 of them: its 264-byte record is fifteen 16-byte name fields followed by one of 24, and the stride scan reports the fifteen as a table once per record. Counting every run as a table counts the same bytes twice, and a reference resolved against the record names the record and the field it picks rather than a position in a grid.

locations.symbol: record array whose interior was read as 20 tables
locations.note: RVA 0x35D640, 264-byte record over 29 records, 16 name fields: fifteen of 16 bytes then one of 24.

locations.symbol: record array whose interior was read as 11 tables
locations.note: RVA 0x4ECCB8, 352-byte record over 49 records, 9 name fields: one of 32 bytes then eight of 40.

records.title: A grid does not stop at the end of a record's field block
records.summary: Nothing stops a constant-stride walk at a field of a different width whose name is short enough to terminate inside the walk's stride, so a run started inside a record keeps going into the next field, the next record, or out of the record array entirely. 87 runs overrun their field block, by 270 elements in total. The 40-byte blocks inside the 352-byte localisation record are the clearest case: the block is seven fields, eleven separate runs claim eight, and the eighth element is the following record's 32-byte field read as though it were 40. The record's field widths repeat with a measured period and are the stronger reading, so the run is cut back to its block. A block shorter than the minimum entry count is kept rather than discarded: the minimum exists to stop a stride hypothesis being reported on a few coincidences, and a block two scans agree on is not a hypothesis.

locations.symbol: run that overran its field block
locations.note: RVA 0x4ED6A0, stride 40, claimed 8 elements; fields 2 to 8 of the record at RVA 0x4ECCB8 are seven 40-byte fields, so the extent is 7.

locations.symbol: run that overran out of its record array
locations.note: RVA 0x361560, stride 16, claimed 48 elements; fields 4 to 15 of the record at RVA 0x35FE68 are twelve 16-byte fields, so the extent is 12.

records.title: Reconciling the two scans loses no reference and reads 18 of them better
records.summary: Cutting the interiors back left references pointing into bytes no run covered, because the matcher checked only the span with the nearest preceding base and an interior sitting inside a record array starts later and now ends sooner. Considering every span that can contain an address, and preferring the record reading, restores all 206 references and moves 18 of them from a grid position to a record and a field: references resolved against a record layout rise from 8 to 26. That the count is exactly restored is the check that the reconciliation removed duplication rather than evidence.

locations.symbol: record reached by references formerly attributed to its interiors
locations.note: RVA 0x4ECCB8 now carries 13 references naming a record and a field, where those references formerly named 10 separate interior runs.
